A click on a colour picks it again, and a click on the one already picked edits it.

## 🐞 Fixed

- **The accent swatches select again.** 1.15.0 removed the separate picker button and replaced it by making every swatch open the picker — and that quietly deleted what the row was for. Choosing a preset became impossible: every click produced a popover and changed nothing, because a picker only reports a colour once you move something in it. Opening one sets no value at all. The claim in 1.15.0's own notes that "the popover applies live on open" was simply wrong, and this is the correction.
- **So the eight do both jobs now.** A click on a colour that is not in force selects it, immediately, with no popover. A click on the one that IS in force opens the picker on it. Every colour stays editable and there is still no ninth control, because reaching the editor costs the click that selects — which anyone about to change a colour was going to make anyway.
- **A colour you mixed yourself is visible in the row.** Nudge a preset into something that is no longer a preset and it used to be applied everywhere and drawn nowhere: no swatch matched it, none was marked, and there was no way back into the picker that made it. It now lives in the slot of the preset it is nearest to — that circle shows it, stays marked, and re-opens the picker on it. Its name becomes the hex value, since a preset's name on a circle that is no longer that preset says less than nothing.
- **The palette row keeps click-to-edit**, and the difference is what the two rows mean rather than an inconsistency: the accent row has one colour in force out of eight, the rainbow palette has all eight in force at once, so there is no selected one to click twice.

## 🎨 Design

- GlimStone **1.7.3**. The swatch behaviour above is written into the language, so the next surface that drops a control because another one can do its job is told to check that the survivor still does its own.

Settings live under **Extension options › Appearance › Accent colour**.
